content_sanskrit: अथ प्रोड्डयनोद्युक्ततुरङ्गमतरङ्गकः । उत्ताण्डव इवोन्मत्तो बभूव स रणार्णवः
padaccheda: अथ । प्रोड्डयनोद्युक्ततुरङ्गमतरङ्गकः । उत्ताण्डवः । इव । उन्मत्तः । बभूव । सः । रणार्णवः
anvaya: अथ (सः) रण-अर्णवः प्रोत्-डयन-उद्युक्त-तुरङ्गम-तरङ्गकः उन्मत्तः उत्-ताण्डवः इव बभूव।
meaning_english: Then, that ocean of battle became like a mad person performing a wild dance, with its waves formed by horses ready to leap upward.
The white arrows resting on the foam of umbrellas were like schools of fish, and the cavities of that ocean were agitated by the surging, restless waves of the cavalry.
It possessed whirlpools of troops carried away by rivers of various weapons, and its great mountains were the shifting backs of herds of intoxicated elephants.
Head-coverings whirled like straw in the whirlpools of hundreds of shining disc-weapons, while the water-like luster of flashing swords was drunk by the clouds of dust.
The masses of soldiers, broken and unbroken, were like boats in the expansion of the shark-shaped battle arrays, and the caves of that ocean echoed with the deep gurgling sound of the turmoil.
The seeds of arrows emerging from fish-shaped arrays were like mustard seeds, and the circles of waves were the flags clipped by the excellent waves of weapons.
The whirlpools resembled clouds formed by the water of weapons, and the army moving in dense fury acted as the massive timi and timiṅgila sea-monsters.
Terrifying with army-waters clad in black iron armor, its ornaments were the troops trapped within the lines of whirlpools formed by headless trunks.
The regions of space were darkened by the mist of arrow-sprays, and a single, dense, rumbling sound absorbed all other noises with its roar.
The spray consisted of fragments of heads tossed up and down, and the wooden debris floating in the whirlpools of circular arrays were the spinning soldiers.

padaccheda: कष्टटाङ्कारकोदण्डकुण्डलोन्मथनोद्भटः । अशङ्कम् । एव । पातालात् । इव । उद्यत्सैनिकोर्मिमान्
anvaya: (सः) कष्ट-टाङ्कार-कोदण्ड-कुण्डल-उन्मथन-उद्भटः पातालात् उद्यत्-सैनिक-ऊर्मिमान् इव अशङ्कम् एव (अभूत्)
meaning_english: The battle emerged boldly, fierce with the agitation of bows bent into circles and emitting harsh twangs, appearing like an ocean rising from the netherworld with waves of soldiers.
It was frothy with endless banners and umbrellas moving to and fro, while the speed of the flowing rivers of blood swept away chariots as if they were uprooted trees.
The battlefield featured great bubbles of blood resembling elephants, and its stream of troops contained horses and elephants moving like aquatic creatures.

padaccheda: ससंग्रामः । अम्बरग्रामः । इव । आश्चर्यकरः । नृणाम् । अभूत् । प्रलयभूकम्पकम्पिताचलचञ्चलः
anvaya: (सः) स-संग्रामः अम्बर-ग्रामः इव नृणाम् आश्चर्य-करः प्रलय-भूकम्प-कम्पित-अचल-चञ्चलः अभूत्
meaning_english: That battle, like a village in the sky, became a source of wonder for men, as unsteady as mountains shaken by the earthquake of universal dissolution (pralaya).
With birds appearing as floating waves and falling elephant-herds as riverbanks, it resounded with the gurgling roars of terrified, deer-like timid soldiers.
The soldiers were broken by hundreds of locust-like flights of arrows; the battle possessed floating waves of śarabha beasts and echoed with their thunderous roars.

padaccheda: चलद्द्विरेफनिर्ह्रादः । रसत्तूर्यगुहागुरुः । चिरात् । सः । सैन्यजलदः । लुठद्भटमृगाधिपः
anvaya: चलत्-द्विरेफ-निर्ह्रादः रसत्-तूर्य-गुहा-गुरुः लुठत्-भट-मृगाधिपः सः सैन्य-जलदः चिरात् (अभूत्)
meaning_english: That cloud-like army finally manifested, humming like swarms of bees, heavy with the cave-like echoes of sounding trumpets, and featuring fallen warriors as lions.
It was a cloud of spreading dust with army-like mountain peaks dissolving, its body filled with falling superior chariots and a circle of blazing swords.
It rained flowers of severed feet, with banners and umbrellas acting as clouds, while excellent elephants fell into the swelling floods of flowing blood-rivers.
That battle became like the end of a kalpa, intent on swallowing the world, with its cities of chariots, flags, umbrellas, and banners overturned and scattered.
The battle shone intensely like the sun with the mass of falling bright weapons, and it scorched the minds of all with the severe agony of departing lives.
The battlefield was dense with continuous showers of arrows from bow-clouds, while the sky was encircled by the flashes of brandished swords resembling streaks of lightning.
In that battle, the mountains of elephant-corpses fell into the rising ocean of blood, and the falling sparks of clashing weapons looked like stars scattered from the sky.
The sky was filled with clouds of weapons and whirlpools of discuses, while the fire of missiles burnt the soldiers, sending them into the next world.
The earth and mountains were covered by the thunderous rain of weapons, and masses of men were crushed by the falling bodies of great elephants resembling mountains.
The earth and sky were hidden by clouds of arrow-showers and army-ranks, as the collision of the great ocean-like armies produced a relentless, fluid commotion.

padaccheda: व्याप्तः । उग्रानिलोद्भूतैः । जलव्यालैः । इव । अचलः । अन्योन्यदलनव्यग्रैः । शस्त्रोत्पातः । इव । उत्थितैः
anvaya: उग्र-अनिल-उद्भूतैः जल-व्यालैः इव, अन्योन्य-दलन-व्यग्रैः उत्थितैः शस्त्र-उत्पातः इव अचलः व्याप्तः (आसीत्)।
meaning_english: The mountain-like battlefield was pervaded by rising weapons like sea-monsters tossed by fierce winds, all intent on mutual destruction.

content_sanskrit: शूलासिचक्रशरशक्तिगदाभुशुण्डीप्रासादयो विदलनेन मिथो ध्वनन्तः । दीप्ता अधुर्दशदिशः शतशो भ्रमन्तः कल्पान्तवातपरिवृत्तपदार्थलीलाम्
padaccheda: शूलासिचक्रशरशक्तिगदाभुशुण्डीप्रासादयः । विदनेन । मिथः । ध्वनन्तः । दीप्ताः । अधुः । दशदिशः । शतशः । भ्रमन्तः । कल्पान्तवातपरिवृत्तपदार्थलीलाम्
anvaya: मिथो विदलनेन ध्वनन्तः शतशः भ्रमन्तः दीप्ताः शूल-असि-चक्र-शर-शक्ति-गदा-भुशुण्डी-प्रास-आदयः कल्प-अन्त-वात-परिवृत्त-पदार्थ-लीलाम् दश-दिशः अधुः।
meaning_english: Clashing and echoing against each other, hundreds of flaming tridents, swords, discuses, arrows, spears, clubs, and mallets whirled in all directions, mimicking the chaotic dance of objects tossed by the winds at the end of a kalpa.
